findings.summary: The runner neither requires an independent PASS receipt nor recomputes the current preflight and gate assessment before creating the consumption marker.
Job paths and BLIND aggregate input inventories are not bound to preregistered digests, so a substituted input set could pass only retrospective hashing.
Historical join and runtime-recovery dependency digests are reported but not compared with frozen expected values before BLIND consumption.
Receipt and sidecar publication lacks a durable completion marker and file and directory fsync boundaries, allowing an orphaned apparent PASS after interruption.
Receipt, sidecar and marker paths are not required to be distinct canonical non-symlink paths inside a dedicated empty output directory.
The contract denominator says path-backed references while the implementation also counts MISSING_RESULT_PATH, so the gate meaning is inconsistent.
Tests do not yet cover forged or stale preflight, review and source substitution, crash publication states, path aliases, concurrency, or full state-rule parity.

positive_findings: The v4 receipt schema excludes runtime values, outcomes, paths, run IDs and candidate-level records.
The HF/HMF action key excludes F and outcome fields.
The preserved historical build_runtime_join_v2.py digest matched the reviewed commit.
required_disposition: Preserve v4 as failed review evidence and remediate only under a new v5 contract, runner and independent review receipt.
